title: Behavioral fidelity covenant for frozen model versions: prompt shapes, outputs, and parameter semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As part of the pinned-version program we need a formal, machine-readable covenant that guarantees behavioral fidelity for frozen (pinned) model versions. This ticket defines the scope, measurable guarantees, telemetry, and rollout criteria for the 'Behavioral Fidelity Covenant' that onboarded models will sign when published as a pinned version.

Why: Customers pin model versions to avoid regressions in prompt/response shape, top-level fields, and parameter semantics (temperature, top_p, system prompt hints). We must provide a clear contract that sets expectations and enables automated gating during model swaps and runtime upgrades.

Scope: covers: (1) Prompt format and accepted parameter names/aliases (schema + normalization); (2) Output envelope (top-level fields, JSON schema, streaming frames order); (3) Semantic parameter effects (e.g., temperature, max_tokens) with tolerance bands; (4) Performance profile publication (latency p50/p95, throughput at configured batch sizes); (5) Regression detection signals and permitted degradation windows.

Definitions: "behavioral fidelity" = preservation of request->response mapping for the conservation of: required keys, output types, canonical tokenization boundary behavior for seeded prompts, and semantics of documented parameters. "Degradation" = measurable divergence beyond acceptance thresholds defined below.

Contract terms (high-level):
- Prompt schema compatibility: pinned versions must accept the currently documented prompt keys and aliases for that model family. New aliases may be introduced only as additive non-breaking entries and must be documented in the model's onboarding artifact.
- Output envelope invariant: pinned models must preserve top-level keys declared in the onboarding manifest. Adding new top-level keys is allowed if they do not alter existing semantics. Removing or repurposing keys is a breaking change.
- Parameter semantic retention: for core parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop), the directional behavior must be preserved (e.g., increasing temperature should not monotonically reduce entropy). The covenant specifies tolerance bands rather than exact numeric matches.
- Performance profile: publish p50 and p95 token latency with 95% CI for canonical workloads and specified batch sizes. Any change >15% regression in p95 for the pinned profile requires a compatibility exemption and customer notification.
- Observable rollback trigger: automated rollback if regression detection signals exceed severity thresholds (see Acceptance Criteria).

Telemetry & evaluation: required signals to be emitted and stored for at least 90 days: request fingerprint (hash of normalized prompt + parameters), top-k outputs, per-request latency, beam/streaming ordering events, and deterministic sampling seeds when applicable. Evaluation harness will compute: schema-conformance rate, top-1 output equality rate on seed testset, KL divergence on token distributions, and latency regressions.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before 'publish pinned version'):
1) Schema conformance >= 99.5% on onboarding testset (field presence and primitive types).
2) Top-1 output equality >= 98% on stable seed set for deterministic-mode prompts; interpretable deviations (e.g., whitespace) accounted by normalization rules.
3) Parameter effect checks: monotonicity tests for at least 3 canonical scalar parameters pass within configured tolerance bands.
4) Performance: p95 latency regression <= 15% vs. declared profile for the default batch size.
5) Telemetry: all required events emitted and ingestion verified to observability backend.
6) Regression tests integrated into CI with a failing gate on major violations.

Test harness & artifacts:
- GitHub PR with regression harness and sample testset: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567
- Onboarding spec (living doc): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Behavioral+Fidelity+Covenant
- Example onboarding manifest schema: drive link in attachments

Rollout plan:
1) Merge PR with harness and unit tests (ENG-87911).
2) Run full regression suite on existing pinned models and generate baseline report (ENG-87912).
3) Publish covenant artifact alongside model manifest for new pinned-version releases.
4) Canary rollout for runtime changes with covenant checks enforced at the model handshake.
5) If covenant gates fail in canary, abort and open incident; if mild degradations observed, create customer-facing advisory and schedule remediation.

Operational Playbook (short):
- On covenant violation, automatic mitigation prioritizes: (a) route affected customers to previous pinned binary; (b) enable read-only mode for problematic endpoints if routing not possible; (c) notify account teams and open an internal incident.
- Post-incident: root-cause analysis, expand regression testset, and consider expanding tolerance bands with cross-functional approval.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strict should the top-1 equality requirement be for generative outputs vs. structured outputs? Proposal: structured outputs (JSON schemas) require near-perfect matching; free-text generative prompts use token-distribution metrics and curated human-review thresholds.
- Data retention for telemetry vs. privacy: we need seeds and normalized prompts for debugging; consider masking PII and documenting retention in the onboarding manifest.
- Who signs the covenant? Proposal: model owner + release engineering + ML research approvals required.

Next steps: finalize numeric tolerance bands, wire the telemetry tags in runtime, and land the regression harness PR.

Links to reference tickets: ENG-12009 (io-normalization harness), ENG-41523 (serve-interface invariants).
acceptance_checks: Top-1 output equality >= 98% for deterministic-mode prompts
Parameter-effect monotonicity tests pass within tolerance bands
p95 latency regression <= 15% vs declared profile
Telemetry ingestion verified for required events

notes: This covenant is intentionally looser for free-form generation to avoid blocking minor stylistic drift while strict for structured outputs used as programmatic interfaces.
We will expose a machine-readable "covenant.json" in the model manifest so runtime and console can automatically validate during rollouts.
Consider exposing an opt-in 'pinned-fidelity-sla' per-customer for enterprise accounts that require stricter thresholds and notifications.
